title: RAG Evaluation
interviewAnswer: Evaluate retrieval and generation separately. Retrieval metrics ask whether relevant evidence was found; generation metrics assess faithfulness, relevance and task success. Human or domain evaluation remains important.
why: RAG can fail in retrieval or generation, so one end-to-end “answer quality” score is insufficient for debugging.
intuition: Ask two separate questions: did we retrieve the right evidence, and did the model use that evidence correctly?
deepDive: Retrieval evaluation uses metrics such as Recall@K, Precision@K, MRR/nDCG depending on labels/ranking needs. Generation evaluation checks faithfulness/groundedness, answer correctness, relevance and citation support. Build a representative evaluation set with answerable and unanswerable queries. LLM-as-judge can scale evaluation but should be calibrated against human judgments and protected from reference leakage.
workedExample: If the correct policy paragraph never appears in top-5 retrieval, prompting cannot fix the answer. If it is retrieved but the answer contradicts it, the generation/prompt/model stage is the problem.
commonMistakes: Using the same LLM-generated synthetic questions as the only evaluation benchmark.
Treating an LLM judge as unquestionable ground truth.
followUps: How do you evaluate unanswerable queries?
production: Maintain regression suites of real user queries, trace retrieved chunks and model outputs, monitor citation/grounding failures, and rerun evaluation when chunking, embeddings, prompts or models change.
